flags-answered.definition-dropped: character | in a cod: §2002:4 defines 'character' in four senses (in a coded character set, in a screen item, in the COBOL character repertoire, in computer storage) and 'coded character set' as "A set of unambiguous rules that establishes a character set" (taken from ISO/IEC 10646-1); 2023 drops these entries and takes the terms from its normative reference ISO/IEC 10646 (§2023:2), in the same sense. cases.reason: The term class national leans on the national category, which is defined differently. 2002 8.5.2.7 item 3 makes every elementary item explicitly or implicitly of usage national category national; 2023 8.5.2.10 has no such item (its item 3 is the GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group). 2002 USAGE SR11 lets a usage-national item be numeric (PIC 9 USAGE NATIONAL) or boolean (PIC 1 USAGE NATIONAL), so by the 2002 text such items are category, hence class, national and admissible as DISPLAY-OF argument-1; in 2023 they are class numeric or boolean and are not. The reader's scope (Table 3 only) missed this. Probe: the compiler refuses both at --std 2002 and at --std 2023 (COBOL1546 citing §2023:15.26.3). The 2002 text conflicts with itself (8.5.2.9 item 1 also makes PIC 9 USAGE NATIONAL numeric); needs an adjudication of the 2002 category of usage-national numeric and boolean items, then a 2002 witness or a 2002 defect note. compiler-at-2002: wrong under the literal 2002 reading.
